sections.explanation: Begin with a bounded question, defined quantities, units, source and assumptions. Choose the simplest supplied relationship that answers it, and identify where it might fail. Compare model and observations using residuals: observed minus predicted. Inspect their size and pattern without treating a small residual as proof of a mechanism. Check dimensions, limiting cases and a hand-worked example before interpreting a graph. This unit combines existing tools and introduces no new physical law.
sections.worked: For a supplied constant-speed model s=2+3t and synthetic observations(0,2),(1,5.1),(2,7.9), predictions are2,5,8 m and residuals0,0.1,−0.1 m. These small discrepancies describe fit to three supplied values; they do not prove constant velocity outside the interval or reveal measurement uncertainty.
